matches.rationale: No finding mentions the inflated FT-HID dataset size (38,364 vs. 9,120). Finding 1 is about an FPS claim, Finding 2 about Rodrigues' formula, and Finding 3 about indoor-only evaluation. None addresses data integrity in Table 1.

Finding 2 identifies the sign error in the Rodrigues rotation formula (1+cosθ instead of 1−cosθ) in Section 3.2, Equation (3), which is exactly the method_logic_consistency issue described in ground truth 2.

No finding reports the omission of batch size, learning rate schedule, warmup steps, etc. The three findings cover FPS misrepresentation, a rotation formula error, and indoor-only subset reporting, none of which relate to missing training hyperparameters.
No finding challenges the 'first egocentric realistic world simulator' claim. Finding 1 addresses the FPS inconsistency, not the exaggerated primacy assertion.
No finding mentions the fabricated Matrix-Game reference or any citation fabrication in the Related Work.

Finding 3 describes how Table 2 and Table 3 present results restricted to indoor scenes without disclosure, exactly the silent subset restriction and misleading performance reporting described in ground truth 6.
No finding mentions an undefined β in the noise schedule. The findings are about FPS, Rodrigues, and indoor-only evaluation.
No finding discusses the asymmetric prompt enrichment (Qwen2.5-VL used for competitors but not PlayerOne). The existing findings address entirely different issues.

No finding addresses the overclaim of 'diverse scenarios' from a 100-video indoor benchmark. Finding 3 is about table-level evaluation manipulation, not rhetorical overreach in the textual claims of Section 4.3.
No finding notes the missing anonymization/ethics statement. The findings address speed, a formula error, and data evaluation, not ethical omissions.
No finding reports the promotional language ('completely solves'). The rhetorical inflation described in ground truth 11 is not covered by any finding.

Finding 1 identifies the contradiction between an abstract claim of real-time/30 FPS generation and the actual 8 FPS speed detailed in later sections, matching the cross-section inconsistency in ground truth 12.
No finding reports a fabricated MPJPE value (98.42 instead of 127.16) in Table 2. Finding 3 discusses the indoor-only subset but not a changed number.
No finding mentions a channel dimension mismatch (e.g., 3 vs 5 channels) in the motion latents. The findings do not address this method_logic_consistency error.

No finding reports the contradiction between the conclusion's claim of coherent generation and the documented limitations on game scenarios. The findings do not cover this claim_interpretation_distortion.
